props.gloss_en: one may roof [the sukkah] with boards -- R' Yehuda
and R' Meir forbids
if one placed on it a board four tefachim wide -- kesheira
provided he does not sleep beneath it
Rav: the dispute concerns boards that have [a width of] four
Rav: for R' Meir holds the decree of the roof, and R' Yehuda does not
Rav: but with boards that do not have four, all agree it is kesheira
Shmuel: the dispute concerns boards that do not have four
Shmuel: but if they have four, all agree it is pesula
under three, all agree it is kesheira -- why? they are merely reeds
where they disagree is from three to four
one master holds: since they are not the measure of a place, we do not decree
the other master holds: since they have left the category of lavud, we decree
two sheets combine
two boards do not combine
R' Meir: boards too are like sheets [they combine]
'combine' means: combine to [the measure of] four [tefachim]
'combine' means: combine to four amot from the side
if he roofed with cedar boards that do not have four, all agree it is kesheira
if they have four, [that is where] R' Meir and R' Yehuda dispute
with four, R' Meir invalidates
and R' Yehuda validates [boards of four]
R' Yehuda: there was an incident in a time of danger when we brought boards that had four, roofed over a porch, and sat beneath them
if he roofed with cedar boards that have four, all agree it is pesula
if they do not have four, [that is where] R' Meir and R' Yehuda dispute
without four, R' Meir invalidates
and R' Yehuda validates [boards under four]
R' Meir concedes that if there is a board's width between board and board, one places psal between them and it is kesheira
R' Yehuda concedes that if one placed on it a board four tefachim wide, it is kesheira, but one does not sleep beneath it, and one who sleeps beneath it has not fulfilled his obligation
if he turned them on their sides: Rav Huna said, pesula
and Rav Chisda and Rabba bar Rav Huna say: kesheira
Rav Nachman: they became like metal skewers

the baraita: a sukkah not holding his head, most of his body and his table; or breached by a breach a kid could leap through headfirst; or on which he placed a board four tefachim wide, even if he brought only three tefachim inside -- pesula
and all psal protruding from the sukkah is judged as the sukkah

deflected_by.gloss_en: אמרו לו: משם ראיה? אין שעת הסכנה ראיה

supports.gloss_en: לימא מסייע ליה: a board four wide, even if only three tefachim were brought inside -- pesula; היכי דמי, לאו כגון שהפכן על צידיהם?

deflected_by.gloss_en: לא, הכא במאי עסקינן -- כגון דאנחה אפומא דמטללתא, דעייל תלתא לגיו ואפיק חד לבר, דהוה ליה פסל היוצא מן הסוכה (= p_psal_hayotze_kasukkah)

objections.gloss_en: אין בהן ארבעה, ואפילו פחות משלשה, הא קנים בעלמא נינהו? -- under four would include under three, and those are merely reeds; why would R' Meir forbid?

answered_by.gloss_en: הכי קאמר: four -- all pasul; under three -- all kasher, mere reeds; they dispute three to four (= p_pappa_machloket_shlosha_ad_arba)

objections.gloss_en: תנן: נתן עליה נסר שהוא רחב ארבעה ... ובלבד שלא יישן תחתיו -- for Shmuel (four is unanimously pasul) that is why one does not sleep beneath it; but for Rav, on R' Yehuda's view boards of four are kasher, so why not sleep beneath it?

answered_by.gloss_en: מי סברת דברי הכל היא? סיפא אתאן לרבי מאיר -- the seifa is R' Meir's alone

objections.gloss_en: תא שמע: שני סדינין מצטרפין, שני נסרין אין מצטרפין, רבי מאיר אומר אף נסרין כסדינין -- for Shmuel 'combine' is to four (14b.2); for Rav, היכי דמי? if each has four, why combine? if not, why forbid -- they are merely reeds! (14b.3)

answered_by.gloss_en: לעולם דאית בהו ארבעה, ומאי מצטרפין -- מצטרפין לארבע אמות מן הצד (= p_mitztarfin_learba_amot_min_hatzad, aliba Rav)

objections.gloss_en: לישנא אחרינא: for Rav, R' Meir's 'combine' is four amot from the side; but for R' Yehuda, who validates even boards of four, what is 'do not combine'? they are merely reeds!

answered_by.gloss_en: איידי דקאמר רבי מאיר מצטרפין, אמר רבי יהודה אין מצטרפין -- the phrase is R' Meir's, echoed by R' Yehuda
